FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Fruits, Vegetable and Allied Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture 
Division Council. 


Vinegar is a natural fermented product known to be produced from suitable raw material of vegetable origin by 
alcoholic and acetous fermentation. Synthetic vinegar is also manufactured by dilution of acetic acid to the required 
concentration. Vinegar is used on the table to flavour and acidify food and also to preserve food. It finds commercial 
use in the manufacture of pickles, sauces, etc. This standard was formulated in 1999 to provide guidance on the 
quality of production of both brewed and synthetic vinegar. It was based on CODEX STAN 162-1987 ‘Codex 
Standard for Vinegar’, published by the Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme, Codex Alimentarius 
Commission, Rome. 


In this revision of standard few changes have been made like definition of vinegar has been elaborated and 
maximum permissible limit for Arsenic has been reduced from | to 0.1 mg/kg for synthetic vinegar, and maximum 
permissible limit of Arsenic, Lead and Copper have been specified for brewed vinegar also. Clause 6.3 has also 
been added to include food additives that may be used in vinegar. 


In the formulation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Food Safety and 
Standards Act, 2006 and the Rules framed thereunder and the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 
2011. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under these, wherever applicable. 


A scheme for labelling environment friendly products known as ECO-Mark has been introduced at the instance of 
the Ministry of Environment and Forests (MoEF), Government of India. The ECO-Mark shall be administered by 
the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) under the BIS Act, 1986 as per the Resolution No. 71 dated 20 February 1991 
as published in the Gazette of the Government of India vide GSR 68(E) dated 8 February 1993. For a product to 
be eligible for marking with the ECO-Mark it shall also carry the Standard Mark of BIS for quality besides 
meeting additional environment friendly requirements. The environment friendly requirements for vinegar have 
also been included in the standard, which are based on the Gazette Notification No. 215(E) dated 17 May 1996 
for Labelling Food Additives as Environment Friendly Products, published by the Government of India. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result ofa test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 14703 : 2017 


Indian Standard 
VINEGAR — SPECIFICATION 
(First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and methods 
of sampling and test for brewed and synthetic vinegar. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below: 


IS No. Title 

695 : 1986 Specification for acetic acid (third 
revision) 

2491 : 2013 Methods for sampling and test for 
processed fruits and vegetables 

2860 : 1964 Methods for sampling and test for 
processed fruits and vegetables 

3752 : 2005 Alcoholic drinks — Methods of test 

7219 : 1973 Method for determination of protein 
in foods and feeds 

7732 : 2003 Apple juice preserved exclusively by 
physical means 

3 DEFINITIONS 


For the purpose of this standard the following 
definitions shall apply: 


3.1 Brewed Vinegar — A product derived from 
alcoholic and acetous fermentation of any suitable 
medium, such as fruits, malt, molasses, jaggary, and 
sugarcane juice etc, with or without addition of caramel 
and spices. 


3.2 Synthetic Vinegar — A substitute for vinegar, 
prepared by dilution of acetic acid, with or without 
addition of caramel and spices which is not the product 
of alcoholic and acetous fermentation. 


4 TYPES 

Vinegar shall be of any of the two types. 
4.1 Brewed Vinegar 

4.2 Synthetic Vinegar 


NOTE — Brewed vinegar shall not be fortified with acetic acid. 


5 REQUIREMENTS 


5.1 Vinegar shall be a clear liquid, free from cloudiness 
or suspended particles. It shall possess the characteristic 
taste and odour of the raw material from which it is 
produced. 


5.2 It shall be free from sulphuric acid or any other 
mineral acid and added colouring matter except 
caramel. 


5.3 Vinegar shall also meet the following requirements 
given in Table 1. 


5.4 In brewed vinegar, when malt is used as a medium 
it shall have atleast 0.05 percent of phosphorus 
pentoxide and 0.04 percent of nitrogen when tested by 
the method prescribed in Annex D and IS 7219 
respectively. 


5.5 When tested by the methods of sampling and test 
prescribed in 18 of IS 2860, the product: 


a) shall be free from micro-organisms capable 
of development under normal conditions of 
storage, 

b) shall not contain vinegar eels or substantial 
quantities of other suspended matters and 
sediments, 

c) shall be free from turbidity caused by micro- 
organisms (mother of vinegar), and 

d) shall not contain any substance originating 
from micro-organisms in amounts which any 
represent a hazard to health. 


5.6 Hygiene 


The product shall be prepared in accordance with the 
hygienic practices prescribed in IS 2491. 


5.7 The product(s) shall comply with requirements of the 
Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards 
and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011 and the Rules 
made thereunder, the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 
and the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 
2011 requirements, etc, wherever applicable. 


6 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR 
ECO-MARK 


6.1 General Requirements 


6.1.1 The manufacturers shall produce to BIS

manufacturer. 


6.1.5 The product package or leaflet accompanying it 
may display instructions of proper use and storage so 
as to maximize the product performance, safety and 
minimize wastage. 


6.2 Specific Requirements 


Vinegar shall conform to the requirements of quality 
prescribed under 5. 


6.3 Additives 


The product covered under this standard may contain 
food additive(s) as per Food Safety and Standards 
(Food Products Standards and Food Additives) 
Regulations, 2011. 


7 PACKING 


7.1 Vinegar shall be packed in a suitable container 
which does not affect the quality of the product. 


8 MARKING 


8.1 The following information shall be marked clearly 
and indelibly on the package:

8.2 BIS Certification Marking 


8.2.0 The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


8.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the 
provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 
and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
details of conditions under which the licence for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 


8.3 ECO-Mark 


The product may also be marked with ECO-Mark, the 
details of which may be obtained from the Bureau of 
Indian Standards. 


9 SAMPLING 


Representative sample shall be drawn in accordance 
with the method prescribed in IS 2860. 


IS 14703 : 2017 


ANNEX A 
[Table 1, SI No. (111)] 
DETERMINATION OF TOTAL SOLIDS 


A-1 APPARATUS 
A-1.1 Hot Air Oven 
A-1.2 Water Bath 


A-1.3 Desiccator — Containing freshly activated silica 
gel or equivalent desiccant. 


A-1.4 Dish — 50 ml capacity, platinum. 
A-1.5 Pipette — 10 ml. 


A-2 PROCEDURE 


A-2.1 Measure 10 ml sample into weighed platinum 
dish. 


A-2.2 Evaporate on boiling water bath for 30 min and 
dry for exactly 2.5 h in an oven maintained at a 
temperature of boiling water 


A-2.3 Cool in a desiccators and weigh. 


A-3 CALCULATION 


100 (M, —M,) 
A3.1 Total solids, percent (m/v) = ~y; 
where 
M, = mass, in g, of dish with total solids; 


M, = mass, in g, of empty dish; and 


V = volume, in ml, of sample taken. 


ANNEX B 
[Table 1, SI No. (iv)] 
DETERMINATION OF TOTAL ASH 


B-1 APPARATUS 
B-1.1 Water Bath 


B-1.2 Muffle Furnace — Maintained at temperature 
of 500-550°C. 


B-1.3 Dish — Platinum. 
B-1.4 Filter Paper — Ashless. 


B-1.5 Desiccator — Containing freshly activated silica 
gel. 


B-2 PROCEDURE 


B-2.1 Measure 25 ml of sample into weighed platinum 
dish. 


B-2.2 Evaporate to dryness on water or steam bath and 
heat in muffle furnace for 30 min at 500-550°C. 


B-2.3 Break up charred mass in platinum dish. Add 
hot water, filter through ashless filter paper and wash 
thoroughly with water. 


B-2.4 Return paper and contents to dish. Dry and heat 
for 30 min at approximately 525°C or until all the 


carbon is burned off. 


B-2.5 Add filtrate, evaporate to dryness and heat for 
15 min at approximately 525°C. 


B-2.6 Cool in desiccator and weigh (M,). 


B-2.7 Reheat for 5 min and cool for approximately 1 h 
in a desiccator. 


B-2.8 Place weight (M,) on balance pan before 
removing dish from dessicator and weigh rapidly to 
nearest mg. 


B-2.9 Preserve the dish for further testing (see D-2.1). 


B-3 CALCULATION 


B-3.1 Total ash (on dry basis), 100 (M, -M,) 
percent u V 


where 
M, 
M, = mass, in g, of empty dish; and 


mass, in g, of dish with ash; 


V = volume of sample taken. 


IS 14703 : 2017 


ANNEX C 
[Table 1, SI No. (v)] 
DETERMINATION OF SOLUBLE SOLIDS 


C-0 PRINCIPLE 


Residual mass of test portion is determined after 
evaporation on water bath followed by oven-drying at 
atmospheric pressure. Total volatilization of acetic acid 
is ensured by repeating evaporation three times after 
restoration to at least original volume with water. 


C-1 APPARATUS 
C-1.1 Pipette — 10 ml. 
C-1.2 Filter Paper — For slow filtering. 


C-1.3 Dishes — 75 mm diameter, platinum, nickel, 
stainless steel, or glass with tight-fitting lids that can 
be readily removed. 


C-1.4 Drying Oven 


C-1.5 Desiccator — Containing freshly activated silica 
gel, or equivalant desiccant. 


C-2 DETERMINATION 


C-2.1 Uncover dish and place dish and its lid in an 
oven maintained at 103°C for 1 h. Place lid on dish 
and transfer covered dish to desiccator. Let the dish 


cool to room temperature and accurately weigh to 
nearest 0.1 mg (M)). 


C-2.2 Shake sample, and filter through paper. Pipette 
10 ml sample into dish. Place dish on boiling water 
bath and evaporate almost to dryness. 


C-2.3 Add 15 ml water to dish and stir with glass rod. 
Wash stirring rod with small amount of water. Evaporate 
almost to dryness on boiling water bath. Repeat the 
step twice. 


C-2.4 Place uncovered dish with its lid in an oven 
maintained at 103°C for 3 h. Cover dish with lid and 
transfer covered dish to desiccator. Let dish cool to 
room temperature, and, as quickly as possible, 
accurately weigh to nearest 0.1 mg (M,). 


C-3 CALCULATION 
100 (M, -M,) 


Total soluble solids, percent (m/v) = y 


where 
M, = mass, in g, of empty dish and lid; 
M, = mass, in g, of dish, lid, and final sample; and 


V = volume, in ml of sample taken 


ANNEX D 
(Clause 5.4) 
DETERMINATION OF PHOSPHORUS PENTOXIDE 


D-1 REAGENTS 


D-1.1 Molybdate Solution — Dissolve 100 g 
molybdic acid (M,O;) in mixture of 144 ml ammonium 
hydroxide (NH,OH) and 271 ml water. Cool and slowly 
pour solution stirring constantly, into cool mixture of 
489 ml nitric acid and 1 148 ml water. Keep final 
mixture in warm place for several days or until portion 
heated to 40° deposits no yellow precipitate. Decant 
solution from any sediment and keep in vessels. 


D-1.2 Acidified Molybdate Solution — To 100 ml 
molybdate solution (D-1.1) add 5 ml nitric acid. Filter 
immediately before use. 


D-1.3 Standard Sodium Hydroxide Solution — 
Dilute 324.03 ml IN alkali, carbonate-free to 1 litre. 


D-1.4 Standard Acid Solution — Prepare solution of 
hydrochloric acid or of nitric acid, corresponding to 


concentration of sodium hydroxide standard solution 
(see D-1.3) or to half this concentration, and standardize 
by titration against sodium hydroxide standard solution 
(D-1.3), using phenolpthalein. 


D-1.5 Phenolphthalein Indicator 
D-1.6 Nitric Acid, Concentrated — Analytical grade. 


D-1.7 Nitric Acid, Dilute (1+8) and (1+3) — Prepared 
by diluting one part by volume of concentrated nitric 
acid (analytical grade) with 8 parts by volume of 
distilled water and 3 parts by volume of distilled water, 
respectively. 


D-2 PROCEDURE 


D-2.1 Dissolve ash (see B-2.9) in approximately 50 ml 
boiling nitric acid (1+8). 


D-2.2 Pippette into a beaker or flask, an aliquot 
corresponding to 0.4 g sample for phosphorus 
pentoxide. Add 5-10 ml nitric acid. Then add 
ammonium hydroxide until precipitate that forms 
dissolves only slowly on vigorous stirring. Dilute to 
75-100 ml, and adjust to 25-30°C. 


NOTE — If sample does not give precipitate with ammonium 
hydroxide as test of neutralization, make solution slightly 
alkaline to litmus paper with ammonium hydroxide and then 
slightly acidic with nitric acid (1+3). 
D-2.3 Add 20-25 ml acidified molybdate solution to 
ensure complete precipitation. Shake or stir 
mechanically for 30 min at room temperature. Decant 
at once through filter paper and wash precipitate twice 
by decanting with 25-30 ml portion water, agitating 
thoroughly and allowing to settle. 


D-2.4 Transfer precipitate to filter paper and wash with 
cold water until filtrate from 2 fillings of filter yields 
pink colour on adding phenolphthalein and 1 drop of 
the standard alkali. 


IS 14703 : 2017 


D-2.5 Transfer precipitate and filter paper to beaker. 
Dissolve precipitate in small excess of standard alkali. 
Add few drops of phenolphthalein and titrate with 
standard acid (D-1.4). 


D-2.6 Express the results as mg of P,O./100 ml vinegar. 
D-3 CALCULATION 
Phosphates as (P;.0,), _ 0.308 8x (VN, -V,N,) 


percent by mass M 
where 

V, = volume, in ml, of standard sodium hydroxide 
solution used; 

N, = normality of the standard sodium hydroxide 
solution used; 

V, = volume, in ml, of standard acid used to 
neutralize alkali; 

N, = normality of standard acid used to neutralize 


alkali; and 


M = mass, ing, of the material taken for test.

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’.
